messages:
Amanda Chen: quick sync — we need to lock down the metrics ingestion contract for per-route SLO dashboards. specifically: TTFT, tokens/sec, and P50/P95/P99 latency buckets. can we sketch labels and retention?
Raj Patel: +1. main questions: what counts as "latency"? total request time vs model generation only vs time-to-first-token (TTFT). also need to decide histogram vs summary.
Leah Kim: runtime perspective: we can emit three distinct metrics from the serving runtime: `runtime.request.duration_ms` (end-to-end), `runtime.generate.first_token_ms` (TTFT), and `runtime.generate.tokens_per_sec`. each should have labels for `model_id`, `route_id`, `route_version`, `region`, and `instance_type`.
Tony Morales: from Console/UX we need P50/P95/P99 panels per route and an aggregated model view. customers expect to pick a time range and see TTFT + tokens/sec heatmap. also want canary vs prod comparison.
Raj Patel: agreed. for SLO math we need quantiles for p50/p95/p99 on latency and TTFT. Prometheus histograms make aggregation easier for percentiles if we expose buckets that match our expected latencies. otherwise we'd need summaries which don't aggregate across dimensions as nicely.
Leah Kim: proposal for histogram buckets for `runtime.generate.first_token_ms`: [1, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000, 3000]. tokens/sec is a gauge sampled per-second average over the request; we can emit `runtime.generate.tokens_per_sec` as a gauge and also emit `runtime.generate.tokens_total` counter for derived rates.
Amanda Chen: sounds good. two more asks: 1) route-level tagging — ensure every request includes `route_id` and `route_version` in telemetry. 2) include `model_variant` label (e.g., fp16-quant, int8) so Optimize can link perf to quantization.
Raj Patel: runtime change needed: add labels to current telemetry header. sample proto snippet: 
```
metric: "runtime.generate.first_token_ms"
labels: {
  "route_id": "string"
  "route_version": "string"
  "model_id": "llama-2-70b"
  "model_variant": "int8"
  "region": "us-west-2"
}
value_ms: 42
```
Leah Kim: implementation note — high-cardinality labels are a risk. `route_id` is okay since number of routes is limited per org, but `model_id` must be normalized (e.g., short ids) and we should avoid user-provided free-text. also we should cap `route_version` cardinality (use semantic version or rollout id).
Tony Morales: console asks: expose a dropdown to surface models or routes with >1% error rate or >SLO breach. we also want a quick link from P99 panel to traces (example IDs). can we include exemplars?
Leah Kim: we can emit exemplars (trace_id) on high-latency events. runtime can attach `trace_id` label as exemplar metadata for the histogram buckets. that'll let dashboards link to traces directly.
Raj Patel: telemetry ingestion: need a contract for ingestion endpoint schema + a validation layer that rejects unknown labels. also retention plan: raw metrics 30d, aggregated rollups (1m/5m) 90d, long-term rollups 1y.
Amanda Chen: product asks for default dashboard templates: per-route SLO (P50/P95/P99 latency, TTFT, tokens/sec), throughput (requests/sec, tokens/sec), and saturation (queue depth, gpu_util). we'll need dashboard jsons in the repo.
Leah Kim: runtime will start emitting the new metrics behind a feature flag. rollout plan: stage=canary -> stage=prod. we'll include `telemetry_flag=route_metrics_v2` label for visibility.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: new runtime with telemetry flag `route_metrics_v2` deployed to canary fleet (canary-1) at 1715004800 — see https://ci.internal/deploy/321
Raj Patel: follow-ups for infra: 1) add ingest validation for allowed labels; 2) ensure histograms are bucketed as proposed; 3) add exemplar support in the metrics pipeline. who's owning the ingest change?
Amanda Chen: Raj + Leah will own runtime changes. Raj will coordinate ingest validations with infra. Tony owns dashboard JSONs and UX. I'll own rollout and docs.
Tony Morales: i'll draft dashboard templates today and post PR by EOD. thinking of panels: 
- TTFT: P50/P95/P99 (per-route dropdown)
- Gen tokens/sec: 95th percentile and trend
- Throughput: requests/sec and tokens/sec heatmap
- Model comparison: grouped by model_variant
Tony Morales: also want a small UX to toggle between absolute ms and relative % SLO breach over baseline.
Raj Patel: infra note: we need to be careful about scrape rate and cardinality. suggest emitting metrics at request end but only for sampled requests at 1/10 for tokens/sec per-request to control ingestion; TTFT and latency we should keep unsampled for accuracy. we can tag `sampled=true/false`.
Leah Kim: runtime can add `sample_rate` label and `sampled` boolean. default sampling for tokens/sec = 10%. we'll add ability to override per-route.
Amanda Chen: action items: 
- Raj: ingest validation PR + sampling config (due by 1715080000)
- Leah: runtime PR to emit new metrics behind flag (due by 1715060000)
- Tony: dashboard JSON templates PR (due by 1715010000)
- Amanda: doc + rollout plan (due by 1715100000)
Amanda Chen: any blockers?
Raj Patel: none from infra, but need exact allowed label whitelist from product for dashboard filtering.
Tony Morales: i'll post whitelist today (route_id, route_version, model_id, model_variant, region, stage).
Leah Kim: one more: we should record TTFT both for cached prefix responses and cold starts separately. suggest label `cache_hit=true/false`.
Amanda Chen: good catch — add `cache_hit` to the contract.
telemetry-bot: ingest-service: schema v2 accepted (preview). examples validated. live in canary.
Amanda Chen: thanks — we'll reconvene after canary metrics stream looks healthy. :thumbsup:
